translationRepairs: He later offended the throne on another matter; an edict called him unlearned, stripped him of Upper Study duty, and demoted him to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
He later offended the throne on another matter; an edict called him unlearned, demoted him to president of the Court of Judicial Review, and stripped him of Upper Study duty.
Chinese 降大理寺卿，罷直書房 lists demotion before dismissal from Upper Study; the idiomatic English reversed those two actions.
After another demotion he became a secretary in the Office of Transmission, then left censor-in-chief and vice minister of War, before leaving the capital as commanding general of Taining.
After another demotion he became a secretary in the Office of Transmission, then Left Vice Censor-in-chief and vice minister of War, before leaving the capital as commanding general of Taining.
左副都御史 is Left Vice Censor-in-chief; the idiomatic English omitted 副 and understated the office.

He was again demoted for an affair to secretary of the Office of Transmission, and served successively as left censor-in-chief and vice minister of War; he went out as commanding general of Taining garrison.

He was again demoted for an affair to secretary of the Office of Transmission, and served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-chief and vice minister of War; he went out as commanding general of Taining garrison.
Same omission of 副 in the literal: 左副都御史 must be Left Vice Censor-in-chief.

In Daoguang 10 (1830) he was posted governor-general of Jilin. He memorialized: "Lands west of the Songhua and north of the Huifa had long been under closure edicts, while other vacant hills were patrolled by guard posts and only garrison troops might hunt for tribute game.

In Daoguang 10 (1830) he was posted General of Jilin. He memorialized: "Lands west of the Songhua and north of the Huifa had long been under closure edicts, while other vacant hills were patrolled by guard posts and only garrison troops might hunt for tribute game.
吉林將軍 is the Jilin banner general, not a governor-general (總督); the proposed title matches the Chinese.

In the tenth year he went out as governor-general of Jilin. In a memorial he said: 'West of the Songhua River and north of the Huifa River are tracts closed by former regulations; elsewhere idle mountain land all had guard posts, and only soldiers were permitted to hunt livestock for tribute items.

In the tenth year he went out as General of Jilin. In a memorial he said: 'West of the Songhua River and north of the Huifa River are tracts closed by former regulations; elsewhere idle mountain land all had guard posts, and only soldiers were permitted to hunt livestock for tribute items.
Literal likewise mistranslates 將軍 as governor-general; General of Jilin is correct.

At Wula Liangshui Spring 73,900-odd shang had been opened; please allocate 20,000 shang east of the Erdos River, seventy percent to the Wula commandant's yamen and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's yamen, as allowances.

At Wula Liangshui Spring 73,900-odd shang had been opened; please allocate 20,000 shang east of the Second River, seventy percent to the Wula commandant's yamen and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's yamen, as allowances.
二道河 is the Second River (Erdao He), not the Erdos River; the proposed place-name matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.

fourth, institute regular inspections—in late spring the Jiancheng intendant would tour Yuexi and Huanbian, the Yongning intendant Ma Bian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each once a year; in autumn the provincial commander and Jiancheng regional commander would split patrols to survey the passes;

建昌道 and 建昌總兵 are Jianchang titles; Jiancheng is a mistransliteration of 建昌.

fourth, schedule regular inspections—between spring and summer each year the Jiancheng circuit intendant should tour Yuexi and Huanbian, the Yongning circuit intendant Ma Bian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each making one full round; in autumn and winter the provincial commander-in-chief and Jiancheng regional commander should divide duties to patrol and survey border passes;

fourth, schedule regular inspections—between spring and summer each year the Jianchang circuit intendant should tour Yuexi and Huanbian, the Yongning circuit intendant Ma Bian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each making one full round; in autumn and winter the provincial commander-in-chief and Jianchang regional commander should divide duties to patrol and survey border passes;
Literal repeats the same 建昌 → Jiancheng error; Jianchang is the correct reading.
fifth, reward frontier officials—the subprefectural judges of Ma Bian and Yuexi, upon completing three years' salary, should be promoted by special selection to vacant prefect posts.
fifth, reward frontier officials—the subprefects of Ma Bian and Yuexi, upon completing three years' tenure, should be promoted by special selection to vacant prefect posts.
同知 are subprefects, not judges, and 三年俸滿 means completing a three-year tenure term, not merely salary.

建昌總兵 is the Jianchang regional commander; Jiancheng mismatches 建昌.

Baoxing argued: 'Ma Bian and Yuexi are far apart; please have the commander-in-chief station in spring and autumn, when tribal bandits appear, at the three subprefectures of Ma Bian, Huanbian, and Leibo, and the Jiancheng regional commander at Yuexi and Ningyue.'

建昌左營 is the Jianchang Left Battalion; Jiancheng is wrong.

An edict ordered the river governor to move to Miaogong before the summer flood season each year and return to Jining after the Start of Winter.
立冬 is the Start of Winter solar term, not the winter solstice (冬至).

He died in Xianfeng 1 (1851); the court honored his past service with first-rank insignia, ministerial burial rites, and the posthumous title Wen.
He died in Xianfeng 1 (1851); the court honored his past service with first-rank insignia, ministerial burial rites, and the posthumous title Wenque.
The chapter OCR loses the second character, while Qing genealogical references identify Jingzheng as 文慤公, confirming the posthumous name 文愨 (Wenque).
When the Jiaqing Emperor died suddenly at Rehe in 1820, Xi'en—present in the inner court—argued that the Daoguang Emperor, who had helped suppress the Lin Qing rebellion, should succeed.
When the Jiaqing Emperor died suddenly at Rehe in 1820, Xi'en—present in the inner court—argued that the Daoguang Emperor, who had merit in quelling disorder, should succeed.
定亂勳 cites merit in quelling disorder and does not name Lin Qing; the idiomatic English invented that personal name.
During the Opium War he was told to prepare Shengjing's defenses.
When the English invaded inland and the coast was on alert, he was ordered to prepare Shengjing's defenses.
英吉利內犯，海疆戒嚴 states an English inland invasion and coastal alert; it does not name the Opium War.

The emperor noted Guanjun had confessed to the beating and concubine, and that his nominees Wei Yuanlang and Qiu Mingtai showed he could still judge talent;
魏元烺 uses 烺 (lǎng); the English given name must be Yuanlang, not Yuanhuang.

The emperor said Guanjun had already confessed to beating runners and buying a concubine, and that his recommendations of Wei Yuanlang and Qiu Mingtai showed his judgment of talent was not wholly wrong;
Literal has the same 烺 → huang error; Yuanlang matches the graph.

He had tutored the Daoguang Emperor's eldest son Yiwei; the emperor praised his teaching.
奕緯 is Yiwei; Yizhi mismatches 緯.

When Guanjun first served in the Upper Study he taught the Daoguang Emperor's eldest son Yiwei; the emperor praised his instruction.
